answer: Interleaved Commitment Ledger.** Agents register by submitting a chain of time-locked micro-transactions that wander across independent validators, each confirming only the prior link. Identities whose commitment paths share a vine of common predecessors are collapsed into one account, so cloning requires rebuilding disjoint histories from scratch. The ledger also charges a karst-style sink fee: every new identity pays a fixed coordination tax proportional to the current graph diameter.
